note: Scores 1-5. Each cell: [score, specific criticism -> concrete fix]. Same model plays all five roles, so reviewer independence is limited. Rejected candidates (P1-C05, P2-C10, P2-C11) are excluded.

NOVELTY: Oracle headroom analyses are standard in sequential decisions; novelty is applying it to tool-call chains where nobody has measured it (E7 probes once). -> Frame it as a measurement contribution and state the null result is publishable.
METHODOLOGY: Forking with K=3 continuations gives a noisy Delta_t; hindsight oracle over noisy Deltas overestimates headroom (winner's curse). -> Use held-out continuations to evaluate the oracle policy, not the samples that chose it.
FEASIBILITY: Needs only a local 4-8B model and offline deterministic When2Tool tools; branching cost ~ (T*2*K) extra runs per instance. -> Cap at 450 train instances per env.
EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN: Single-decision oracle must be defined per instance AFTER seeing outcomes or it is a strawman. -> Define it as the best of {never, always, per-instance best pattern} chosen with hindsight; report both.
SKEPTIC: E7 already shows high multi-hop AUROC; headroom may be ~0 on these envs because difficulty is fixed per task. -> Include HotpotQA/MuSiQue-style data where intermediate answers change need, and pre-register the 2-point threshold.

NOVELTY: Two-head probe resembles LNE+LUE (E12) at step level; difference is steps and heads trained on branched labels. -> State explicitly that the delta over E12 is step-level labels from P1-C01.
METHODOLOGY: Subtracting two probabilities from separate heads inflates variance; shared hidden state makes errors correlated in unknown direction. -> Add a direct Delta regression head as ablation; use L2-regularised logistic heads.
FEASIBILITY: Linear heads on cached hidden states train in seconds (E34); the cost is generating branched labels. -> Reuse P1-C01 data.
EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN: Baseline set is good, but a need-probe trained on the same branched data is required to isolate 'utility vs need'. -> Add 'need-probe on identical tasks' and 'oracle-feature' upper bound.
SKEPTIC: E12: utility estimation is weak even at instance level; step-level will be noisier. -> Report AUROC of Delta-sign per step and stop if it is not above need-probe.

NOVELTY: Regret-weighted loss transferred from CAM-DF (E17) to a different decision; transfer, not a new mechanism. -> Be explicit; novelty rests on the call/no-call-in-reasoning application.
METHODOLOGY: Sampling lambda per example makes the target vary with lambda; sign(Delta - lambda*c) is only well-defined if Delta labels are low-noise. -> Use soft targets from K-sample means and a margin band where weight -> 0.
FEASIBILITY: Small MLP/logistic on cached features. -> Share the branched data.
EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN: Needs a matched comparison with two-head subtraction at equal parameters and data. -> Fix feature dimension and training steps.
SKEPTIC: May simply match two-head probes; 'regret' gains vanish when labels are noisy. -> Include a noise-injection sweep.

NOVELTY: Offline RL over probe features for tool calls is a plausible extension of CTA's sequential view (E14).
METHODOLOGY: Fitted-Q with ~10^3 branched trajectories and 3-step horizon is data-starved; off-policy error and distribution shift between branching and learned policy are unaddressed. -> Restrict to tabular/linear Q and compare to one-step rule.
FEASIBILITY: Implementable but fragile; tuning heavy. -> Do only on 3-hop synthetic envs.
EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN: Gain over one-step requires chains where early calls change later necessity; envs may not have that. -> Check with C01 headroom first.
SKEPTIC: 3 hops is too short for dynamic programming to matter.

NOVELTY: Conformal calibration for tool-call decisions is not found in the matrix, but E30 is abstract-level only.
METHODOLOGY: Hops within one trajectory are dependent, so per-step exchangeability fails (S2). -> Calibrate at trajectory level: threshold chosen so the fraction of TRAJECTORIES with any skipped necessary call <= epsilon (instances are exchangeable).
EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN: Coverage vs epsilon plus U cost is a clean test.
SKEPTIC: Trajectory-level guarantee may force near-always-call at small epsilon, erasing savings.

NOVELTY: Cascade of a known probe with a fallback is an engineering combination. -> Only keep if it shows robustness gains, not speed.
METHODOLOGY: Margin m is a free parameter; selecting it on test data leaks. -> Pick m on validation by U-AUC.
EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN: Speed benefit is negligible given E34, so the metric must be U-AUC, not latency.
SKEPTIC: A trivial combination of two existing techniques; likely to be dominated by pure step-wise probing.

NOVELTY: Cross-tool transfer of utility probes is not covered in E13 (which lists a single fixed representation).
METHODOLOGY: Tool embedding learned from three tools is underdetermined; leave-one-out leaves two training tools. -> Use tool descriptors (text embedding of the tool description) instead of free vectors.
FEASIBILITY: Needs three envs: available in When2Tool.
EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN: 'Above chance' is too weak a hypothesis. -> Compare to a per-tool probe trained on the held-out tool with 10% data.
SKEPTIC: Necessity causes differ per tool (E10); transfer will likely fail between knowledge and computation tools.

NOVELTY: Label-definition ablation, largely subsumed by C01/C02.
METHODOLOGY: Clear controlled comparison.
EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN: Hop-local labels require per-hop gold answers; only some envs have them. -> Restrict to When2Tool chains.
SKEPTIC: Reviewers would call this an ablation, not a contribution.

NOVELTY: Cost-conditioning robustness is essentially what When2Tool's tau sweep and To Call or Not to Call's budgets show.
METHODOLOGY: Out-of-range lambda tests extrapolation of the threshold only if the score is calibrated. -> Report calibration.
EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN: Clear.
SKEPTIC: Likely trivially true for any calibrated score: no insight.

NOVELTY: Compares two actuation modes already described in E6 and E14.
METHODOLOGY: Prefill vs in-context depends on chat template and model; results will not generalise. -> Evaluate on two backbones.
EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN: Needs fixed estimator; fine.
SKEPTIC: Engineering ablation.

NOVELTY: Direct comparison of hidden-state vs token-probability features for step-level tool utility is not in the matrix.
METHODOLOGY: Clean feature ablation.
EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN: Add combined features.
SKEPTIC: Expected answer (hidden states win) is unsurprising.

NOVELTY: Closest: CTA (E14-E16) with global p_ret; the per-query p_tool is the delta. Not claimed beyond that.
METHODOLOGY: p_tool_hat trained from query features risks learning dataset artefacts (e.g. entity popularity) rather than tool benefit. -> Group-split by topic/entity for validation.
FEASIBILITY: Sentence-encoder + logistic; labels from running tools on training queries.
EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN: Must charge sampling cost for p_direct signals inside U. -> Report U with and without cost.
SKEPTIC: E12: even with hidden states utility estimation barely helps; with only query text it may not beat a global constant.

NOVELTY: Cheap-preview value-of-information is not in the matrix; links to classical VOI.
METHODOLOGY: Preview features differ per tool; no single method. -> Define a tool-agnostic interface: preview(x) -> feature vector.
FEASIBILITY: BM25 scores are free for the retrieval scenario; calculator parse size is trivial.
EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN: Net utility after preview cost is the correct metric. -> Add 'oracle preview' upper bound.
SKEPTIC: For the calculator and reasoner scenarios previews may be uninformative; gains likely confined to retrieval.

NOVELTY: Sequential testing for sampling-based uncertainty is known in other contexts; applying it to tool-call decisions with cost-conditioned stopping is not in the matrix.
METHODOLOGY: SPRT needs a likelihood model of agreement; use a Beta-Binomial posterior over p_correct with a decision boundary at lambda*c.
FEASIBILITY: Sampling API only; works with black-box.
EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN: Clean: samples per query, U net of cost vs fixed k.
SKEPTIC: Savings may be small if most queries are ambiguous.

NOVELTY: Proxy probing for black-box targets not found.
METHODOLOGY: Knowledge boundaries are model-specific; a proxy's hidden states reflect the proxy's knowledge (S2 flagged). -> Reject unless transfer is tested against query-text baselines first.
EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN: Needs strong text-only baseline.
SKEPTIC: Likely reduces to query-difficulty prediction.

NOVELTY: Diagnostic study of a gap (G15); no new method.
METHODOLOGY: Stratified analysis is sound.
EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN: Clear.
SKEPTIC: Diagnostic only; a reviewer may ask for a fix.

NOVELTY: Guaranteed accuracy floor for tool skipping not found; conformal methods exist (E30).
METHODOLOGY: Single-decision exchangeable queries make split-conformal valid; need a bounded-loss formulation (risk control, not coverage). -> Use a Learn-then-Test-style procedure on accuracy loss.
EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN: Empirical guarantee check on repeated splits.
SKEPTIC: Guarantee may force always-call at tight epsilon; savings are the real question.

NOVELTY: Calibration under shift is well studied; tool-call application is thin novelty.
METHODOLOGY: Sound.
EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN: Shifts: TriviaQA->PopQA/NQ.
SKEPTIC: General calibration result dressed as tool-calling.

NOVELTY: Query routers exist (E35).
METHODOLOGY: Same artefact risk as P2-C01.
EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN: Useful as zero-cost baseline.
SKEPTIC: Probably dominated; best as a baseline.

NOVELTY: Close to CTA's verbalized confidence; two numbers is a small extension.
METHODOLOGY: Overconfidence (E27) may make p_tool uninformative.
EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN: Needs calibration on a held-out set.
SKEPTIC: Models cannot know how well a retriever will do.

NOVELTY: Cross-model disagreement for tool decisions not found, but ensemble disagreement is classical.
METHODOLOGY: Disagreement mixes difficulty and model quality. -> Control with model-pair choice.
FEASIBILITY: Costs a second model; charge it.
EXPERIMENTAL_DESIGN: Needs cost-matched comparison with extra self-samples.
SKEPTIC: Same cost could buy more self-samples (P2-C03), likely better.
